description: Bundle-size budget churn had two root causes: (1) agents budgeting gzip from Vite's build-log reporter, which gzips ~2KB COOLER than scripts/check-bundle-size.ts (Node zlib level 6) — the actual CI gate; (2) stale src/ui/node_modules building a different bundle than CI's fresh install, mistaken for macOS<->Linux drift. Never hand-edit budgets or trust Vite's gzip number.
resolution: build:ui now installs --frozen-lockfile so a clean local build is byte-identical to CI (verified same hash 583998raw/173931gzip); added check-bundle-size.ts --update to re-baseline budgets from the measured build (measured+small headroom), refusing to RAISE unless WARREN_BUNDLE_SIZE_ALLOW_RAISE=1. Budget gzip js set to honest CI floor 174300 (bundle genuinely gzips to 173931 — the framer-motion motion layer — so it could not be ratcheted lower).

content: Pin bun across all GitHub Actions via a repo-root .bun-version file (single source of truth) plus explicit 'with: bun-version-file: .bun-version' on every oven-sh/setup-bun@v2 step (ci.yml, ci-postgres.yml, release.yml, bundle-size-autoheal.yml). Keeps Vite/esbuild minified output — and thus measured bundle-size budgets — reproducible; bump the version deliberately and re-run 'bun run check:bundle-size:build --update' at the same time. Match the version local devs run.

description: release.yml cut GitHub releases with gh release create under GH_TOKEN=github.token; GitHub suppresses workflow runs for events created by the default GITHUB_TOKEN, so deploy-gke.yml's 'release: [published]' trigger never fired and production stayed on the prior version (warren-cb81).
resolution: Removed the release: [published] trigger; deploy-gke.yml now exposes workflow_call(sha,deploy) and release.yml calls it directly via 'uses: ./.github/workflows/deploy-gke.yml' with the released github.sha + secrets: inherit. Build/checkout/tags use inputs.sha (env TARGET_SHA) so the exact release SHA is deployed, plus a post-rollout step verifies the live image tag matches. Guarded by scripts/deploy-trigger.test.ts.

content: Workflow YAML guards live in scripts/*.test.ts: js-yaml for structure, extract the step's run string and execute under bash -c with a PATH-stubbed curl for behavior. Both .test.ts and scripts/** are outside jscpd's src/** pattern, so helper duplication across guard files is free.

title: Secret-expiry heartbeats are sibling jobs
rationale: Visible as a red X but never blocking the release it watches

description: Raw-text token-absence assertions are satisfied by comments
resolution: Assert on the parsed YAML (comments dropped), not the raw workflow text

description: Scenario 39's mutating-route floor is a hand-maintained tripwire that must move with the route table: deleting a POST/DELETE route (warren-5652 removed POST /agents/refresh) fails acceptance-public with 'expected at least N mutating routes' until the floor drops. Root cause of red main was compounding: acceptance-public and ci-postgres ran on PRs but only 'ci' was a required status check, so enable-auto-merge landed PR #646 with acceptance-public already failing.
resolution: Confirmed the drop was a deliberate deletion by diffing API_ROUTE_POLICIES between a5fd59ae and 66e9b5e8 (exactly one entry removed, 14 survivors all still admin/dispatch), then lowered the floor to 14 and extracted it to MIN_MUTATING_BLOCKED_ROUTES so check and message can't disagree. Never lower the floor just to green CI. Added acceptance-public and ci-postgres to main's required status checks via PATCH on the required_status_checks sub-resource (not a full PUT, which would reset omitted protection settings).

description: Pre-commit hook running check:all inside a .claude/worktrees agent worktree can corrupt the worktree git state: core.bare flips to true AND the checked-out branch ref gets moved onto pr.test.ts fixture commits ('base'/'pr'), emptying the index so everything shows untracked.
resolution: git config core.bare false, then git reset --mixed <origin/main sha> (never --hard — working-tree edits survive), verify git status shows only your edits, then commit with --no-verify after running gates manually.

description: warren-cfa7 leakage confirmed live on a dev machine: a sandboxed test run had written fixture identity user.name=test / user.email=test@example.com into the invoking repo's local .git/config. Symptom: 5 host-identity tests fail locally (src/workspace/git/identity.test.ts, materialize.test.ts) because readHostGitIdentity picks up the repo-local fixture config, while CI stays green; commits made from that checkout are authored as 'test'.
resolution: Immediate repair: git config --local --unset user.name && git config --local --unset user.email (host global config takes over; all 5 tests pass). Durable fix — fixture isolation in the test harness — belongs to warren-cfa7.

title: No hardcoded deployment identity in a public self-hosted tree
rationale: Any real name/email/login baked into code or workflows pins every self-hoster's deployment to the maintainer's identity (or, worse, to an unowned domain like the old warren@os-eco.dev). Env vars and repo variables keep identity per-deployment; RFC 2606 .invalid defaults attribute to nobody.

name: hermetic-git-fixtures
description: Test git fixtures must sever inherited repo-context env at the spawn site and pin the discovery ceiling; never rely on per-suite beforeEach env clearing
